context.body: The bounded canonical source is Isaiah 40:1–11; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A voice announces comfort, completed warfare, prepared way, enduring word, good news, divine rule, and shepherd care.
observations.label: Comfort is spoken to a people after judgment: action

observations.body: the city is called to announce God’s arrival without fear.
observations.label: Comfort is spoken to a people after judgment: response

payload.posture: Read Isaiah 40:1–11 as prophets accuse and promise evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The proclamation speaks restoration as certain while the people’s external circumstances are not yet fully changed.
payload.title: Comfort is spoken to a people after judgment
